newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's extends timetable for Names' deposit rise.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's extends timetable for Names' deposit rise.

text.p: Lloyd's of London said on Tuesday it was extending the timetable for planned changes to the amounts of capital Names must provide to support their underwriting activities.
The plans are part of a package of measures to strengthen the financial secuity that underpins Lloyd's.
It is also designed to provide a level playing field between Names - the traditional backers of the insurance market - and corporate members first introduced in 1994.
Names are to be given three years before they have to meet the new requirements to show evidence of assets amounting to 50 percent of premiums underwritten.
A Lloyd's working party last month proposed a two-year transition period but, after consultations, Lloyd's has decided to give Names more time to comply, extending the timetable to the year 2000.
A rise in Names' minimum level of means to 350,000 pounds ($571,000) has also been extended by three years to five years and will come into force in 2002.
This is made up of funds held at Lloyd's and evidence of "other personal wealth" (OPW).
Proposals to double the OPW requirements for 2000 and beyond have been dropped in favour of slightly higher requirements for funds held at Lloyd's.
At present Names must put up between 20 and 30 percent of underwriting capacity compared with 50 percent for corporate members.
By 2000 Names will have to hold 40 percent of premium capacity at Lloyd's with OPW making up a further 10 percent, bringing them into line with corporate members.
In addition, allowances in reaching these levels are being made for Names who have fallen below the minimum levels of capital as a results of the huge losses run-up by Lloyd's between 1988 and 1992.
The use of "principal private residences" as collateral for members' underwriting are to be allowed to continue but only for those in existence at the end of 1994.
Risk assessment is to be extended to all members from 1998 onward and may require higher capital levels for members with greater risk exposure.
